clue.text: This consequence 'certain': a clue CND might compose?

definitions.text: This consequence 'certain': a clue CND might compose?

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are arranged afresh into the answer

parts.note: used as written
used as written; CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament

explanation.surface: A setter imagines the disarmament campaigners writing a puzzle clue about the outcome they fear most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might compose' signals the rearrangement of CERTAIN + A CLUE CND; the whole clue also describes the answer, since CND's warnings are about exactly this kind of disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: CND campaigned against nuclear power and weapons, and a reactor disaster is the consequence they warned would follow.

clue.text: Rivals character or friend held up by plan

indicators.note: the plan word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words before it are written bottom to top

parts.note: used as written
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend is kept in the dark by some scheme, perhaps a rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rivals' is capitalised as a sentence start to hide the title of Sheridan's comedy The Rivals; 'up' turns 'or friend' bottom to top, giving LAPRO; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Malaprop, famous for comic word misuse, is a character in Sheridan's play The Rivals.

clue.text: "Nothing doing!" (Tricky Dick)

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
on means happening or taking place, as in what's on

explanation.surface: A curt refusal is attributed to a sly fellow called Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tricky Dick was the nickname of the US president who resigned over Watergate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky Dick was the derisive nickname given to the 37th US president.

clue.text: See 27 Across
Woman in first bed

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
A denotes first, as in an A grade or class A

explanation.surface: A woman is lying in the first bed of a ward or dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female first name.

clue.text: Woman beds 00700,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Woman beds 00700, (9)': the word for NOB is garbled by OCR and the clue ends in a stray comma, so a cross-reference may be lost; no scan to read it from.

clue.text: Rings Anglo-German couple

parts.note: an English woman's name, Ann
a German man's name, Uli, short for Ulrich

explanation.surface: A pair of English and German partners exchange wedding rings.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple are two names: English ANN and German ULI.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the plural of annulus, a ring-shaped figure or part.

clue.text: I shall determine outcome,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'I shall determine outcome, (5,4,6)': the anagram of I SHALL DETERMINE is clear but the clue ends in a stray comma and has no definition, so its cross-reference to another light appears lost.

clue.text: Mate outside managed single fuel source

indicators.note: the mating word is placed around the other two pieces

parts.note: to unite is to mate or join
ran means managed, as in ran a business
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A partner who runs things on their own is said to be fuelling something.
explanation.definitionFit: Uraninite, or pitchblende, is the chief ore of uranium and so a source of nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Unfinish'd Richard had this idea

indicators.note: Shakespeare's Richard III calls himself unfinish'd; here the word cuts off the end of the deformity

parts.note: Shakespeare's Richard III is portrayed with a ... back

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's misshapen king is turned into a notion he had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinish'd' quotes Richard III's opening speech ('Deform'd, unfinish'd') and removes BACK from the end of his famous hunched back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunch is an intuitive idea or suspicion.

clue.text: Voltaire's the first note by nonsense author

parts.note: le is French for the, the language of Voltaire
A is the first note of the musical scale
cock, as in poppycock, means nonsense

explanation.surface: A French writer's opening note is placed beside a writer of nonsense verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense author' looks like the definition (Lear, Carroll), but nonsense is COCK and author alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Leacock was a Canadian humorist and writer, so he fits as an example of an author.

clue.text: Harrow gave you an education in the common tongue?

indicators.note: the phrase is said in everyday non-rhotic speech, where it sounds like the answer

parts.note: to have educated you is to have taught you

explanation.surface: Harrow, the English public school, seemingly taught its pupil in plain everyday language.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school, but here it is the verb meaning to distress. In common southern English, 'taught you' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow someone is to distress them acutely, a synonym of torment.

clue.text: Muslims besieged here are without cold water

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word are sits around the other piece

parts.note: C marks the cold-water tap

explanation.surface: Besieged Muslim defenders are said to have gone without cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre, in present-day Israel, was a city held by Muslim forces and besieged by the Crusaders in 1189-91.

clue.text: Life processes mobile mast disrupted

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mobile phone mast has been knocked out of action, interfering with life.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the set of chemical reactions that sustain a living organism.

clue.text: Turn, climb, one down here

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle or key
to scale is to climb

explanation.surface: Instructions for a climber: twist, go up, and one person falls here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one down' is a cross-reference to 1 Down: the place where such a disaster occurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscale in Cumbria was the site of Britain's worst reactor fire, in 1957, a nuclear accident.

clue.text: Iodine found in fruit becomes relevant

indicators.note: the iodine is found inside the fruit word

parts.note: apples are a fruit
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemist discovers iodine in fruit, and it suddenly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: If a rule applies, it is pertinent to the case in hand.

clue.text: Wages vote taken round Scots town

indicators.note: the vote word is taken round the town, enclosing it

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Workers vote on pay in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A payroll is the total sum of wages a company pays its staff.

clue.text: After fish, energy that's our zip!

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
a cod is a fish
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: After a fish meal, someone boasts of their zip and vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like energy or vigour, but it is the US ZIP code; 'our' makes it the British counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: The British postal code does the same job as the American ZIP code.

clue.text: Three tragedies easier to unravel

indicators.note: to unravel is to undo and loosen, so these letters are untangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Three tragic plays are said to be simpler to puzzle out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oresteia is Aeschylus's trilogy of Greek tragedies about the house of Atreus.

clue.text: Tudors Club throws out violent shower

indicators.note: throws out suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A historical society for Tudor fans ejects a rowdy bunch of members.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden, very heavy downpour of rain.

clue.text: Being distant a Piscean trait?

definitions.meaning: aloof, cool and stand-... in manner
a quality belonging to the fish, the sign of Pisces

explanation.surface: Coolness and reserve are presented as a typical characteristic of those born under Pisces.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish means aloof, and split as 'of fish' it describes something belonging to the fish of Pisces.

clue.text: Having an advantage, go for economic improvement

parts.note: up means ahead or with the edge, as in two goals up
a turn is a go, as in your turn

explanation.surface: An advantaged player takes a go in the hope of better economic fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise or recovery in business or the economy.

clue.text: House after split?

parts.note: a dwelling that is half of a divided pair, or a building left after a division into two

explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, one of a pair joined by a shared wall.

clue.text: Poet's bloody language? The opposite

indicators.note: instead of the poet holding bloody language, the opposite: the words bloody language hold the poet

explanation.surface: A poet's swearing is called bloody language, or perhaps just the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's bloody language' suggests the poet contains the words; 'The opposite' says the words contain the poet, run across 'bloody language'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet, often called simply by his first name.

clue.text: Loss expert the receiver for chemical company

indicators.note: the expert word acts as the receiver that takes in the company

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, the British chemical giant

explanation.surface: A specialist is called in as official receiver for a failing chemicals firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the receiver' suggests insolvency, fitting 'Loss', but here it means the piece that takes the company inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall, the amount by which spending exceeds income.

clue.text: Like underground chapel clubs, partly demolished

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A subterranean chapel is described as having had its clubs partly knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' looks like it modifies 'demolished', but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptal means relating to a crypt, the chamber beneath a church.

clue.text: Pinched from Decameron as a line

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A line has been stolen from Boccaccio's Decameron.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinched voice sounds strained and through the nose, the quality the answer describes.

clue.text: Risk associated with uranium core in meltdown?

definitions.text: Risk associated with uranium core in meltdown?

indicators.note: a meltdown is a collapse into disorder, used as a noun so the letters before it are thrown together
the core of a word is its central letter

parts.note: used as written

explanation.surface: A warning about the danger of a reactor core melting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder: RISK ASSOCIATED plus N (the middle of URANIUM) plus IN, rearranged by the noun 'meltdown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure to high doses of ionising rays after a reactor accident causes this illness, a real danger of meltdown.
